questions.q: Title: "Describe a market at closing time." Which response best fits the task?
options: A story about a theft and a chase through the stalls
A list beginning "I can see… I can hear…"
An argument about why markets matter
Sensory detail of stallholders packing up as the light fades
questions.why: Description builds a picture and atmosphere; drifting into a plot limits the content mark.

questions.q: How are the 40 composition marks split?
options: 24 content and structure + 16 style and accuracy
16 content and structure + 24 style and accuracy
questions.why: Style and accuracy carry the larger share (24).

questions.q: Which sentence best avoids cliché and uses a precise verb?
options: The rain was as cold as ice.
It was a dark and stormy night.
The big, wet, cold, heavy rain fell.
questions.why: A precise verb is fresher than clichés or chains of adjectives.

questions.q: Name two structures you could use for a descriptive composition.
questions.model: Any two: zoom (wide view to close-up detail); time shift (same place at different times); walk-through; circular (ending echoes the opening).
points: e.g. zoom, time shift, walk-through, circular
